extracted.intended_audience: members of the public, regulated entities, and regulatory practitioners who may submit or advise on comments to this Department of the Air Force interim final rule
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance about submitting public comments on the DAF interim final rule rescinding 32 CFR part 989, and the agency's legal justifications for dispensing with prior notice-and-comment and for immediate effectiveness. Includes procedural submission instructions, public-posting policies, and statutory/precedential criteria bearing on whether notice-and-comment is required.

rubrics_metrics.name: Comment deadline / timeliness
rubrics_metrics.description: This interim final rule is effective July 1, 2025. Comments must be received on or before July 31, 2025.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Commenters have 30 days from the date of publication to submit comments. Comments received before the close of the comment period are available for viewing on regulations.gov (see 'Inspection of Public Comments').

rubrics_metrics.name: Methods and identification for submitting comments
rubrics_metrics.description: You may submit comments, identified by docket number and/or Regulation Identifier Number (RIN), by any of the following methods: Federal eRulemaking Portal (http://www.regulations.gov) or mail to the Department of Defense address provided.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Follow the instructions on regulations.gov for submitting comments. Include the docket number and/or RIN to ensure the comment is associated with this rulemaking. Mail submissions should be addressed to the specified DoD/DAF Regulatory Directorate address.

rubrics_metrics.name: Public availability and posting of comments
rubrics_metrics.description: All comments received before the close of the comment period are available for viewing by the public at http://www.regulations.gov. Comments are posted as soon as possible after they have been received.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Follow the search instructions on regulations.gov to view public comments. Agencies review all submissions and may choose to redact, or withhold, certain submissions (or portions thereof). Submitted comments may not be available to be read until the agency has approved them.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prohibited content (threats and harm)
rubrics_metrics.description: DAF will not post public comments that make threats to individuals or institutions or suggest that the commenter will take actions to harm an individual.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Such comments will be excluded from public posting. The rule states the agency will only post acceptable substantive comments; threatening language is explicitly disallowed for posting.

rubrics_metrics.name: Posting preference for substantive unique comments
rubrics_metrics.description: DAF will post acceptable substantive comments from multiple unique commenters.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The agency indicates a focus on substantive inputs and implies filtering of duplicative or non-substantive submissions; commenters should aim to provide substantive, original input. The agency may redact or withhold submissions as it deems appropriate.

rubrics_metrics.name: Notice-and-comment not required for procedural rules (APA exemption)
rubrics_metrics.description: Notice-and-comment procedures are not required for 'rules of agency organization, procedure, or practice' under 5 U.S.C. 553(b)(A).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: DAF characterizes its NEPA implementing procedures as procedural—detailing structure of EISs, submission requirements, timing of comment periods—so their repeal falls within the APA exception and does not require notice-and-comment. Prior use of notice-and-comment does not bind the agency when notice-and-comment is not required for repeal (Perez v. Mortg. Bankers Ass'n).

rubrics_metrics.name: Interpretative rules and general statements of policy are exempt
rubrics_metrics.description: Interpretative rules (which interpret a statute rather than creating enforceable rights/obligations) and general statements of policy are exempt from notice-and-comment under 5 U.S.C. 553(b)(A).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples: definitions in Appendix A may be interpretative; prefatory sections may be general statements of policy. If parts of the regulation fit these categories, their repeal likewise may not require notice-and-comment.

rubrics_metrics.name: Good-cause findings to bypass notice and delay
rubrics_metrics.description: The APA permits agencies to issue regulations without notice and public comment when the agency finds, for good cause, that notice and comment is 'impracticable, unnecessary, or contrary to the public interest' (5 U.S.C. 553(b)(B)), and to make a rule effective immediately for good cause (5 U.S.C. 553(d)(3)).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: DAF finds good cause because its prior procedures were crafted to supplement now-rescinded CEQ regulations and continuing to operate under them is untenable; therefore immediate rescission is necessary for speed and certainty. Agencies invoking good cause should explain why notice/delay would be impracticable, unnecessary, or contrary to the public interest.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of precedent (Seven County) to characterize NEPA as procedural
rubrics_metrics.description: The Supreme Court in Seven County Infrastructure Coalition v. Eagle County held that 'NEPA is a purely procedural statute' and 'does not mandate particular results, but simply prescribes the necessary process' for environmental review.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: DAF relies on this precedent to justify treating its NEPA implementing regulations as procedural (and thus removable without notice-and-comment). Agencies relying on case law should cite relevant holdings and explain how they affect the characterization of rules as procedural versus substantive.

rubrics_metrics.name: Treatment and weighing of asserted reliance interests
rubrics_metrics.description: DAF acknowledges third-party reliance interests in existing procedures but concludes such reliance interests are 'outweigh[ed]' by other interests and policy concerns; reliance interests grounded in substantive environmental concerns 'are not in accord with the best meaning of the law and are entitled to "no . . . weight."' (citing precedent).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When repealing procedural rules, an agency should identify potential reliance interests and explain why those interests do or do not preclude immediate repeal (e.g., by weighing them against the public interest in prompt conformity to new legal landscape).

rubrics_metrics.name: Agency determination of regulatory impacts under other statutes and EOs
rubrics_metrics.description: The agency must state determinations under Executive Orders and statutes (e.g., Executive Orders 12866/13563 on regulatory review, Executive Order 14192 on deregulatory actions, Congressional Review Act, Paperwork Reduction Act, Regulatory Flexibility Act, Unfunded Mandates Reform Act, Federalism (EO 13132), and Tribal consultation (EO 13175)).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The rule must report OIRA significance determinations, whether the action is deregulatory or major, whether it contains information collection requirements, economic impacts on small entities, unfunded mandates, federalism implications, and tribal effects. These determinations justify compliance (or exemptions) with cross-cutting statutes and EOs and inform both agency choices and public comment.
